1d232uv: This week you review your two classes on **relative clauses**: with **que** to say which person or thing, and with **donde, cuando** and **lo que** for places, moments and ideas. The situation: Daniel, a student from Lima, spends a semester in Santa Ana with the Morán family and learns to find his way around his new neighbourhood.
w6pfun: Que: a detail to say which one
vf4w9y: Sometimes a noun alone is not enough: _la vecina_… which neighbour? With **que** you add a detail that identifies her: _la vecina **que vive enfrente**_. That way you join two ideas in one sentence and don't repeat the noun.
w9b86a: There are two cases. If the noun **does** the action, the verb comes right after _que_: _el señor **que vende** tortillas_. If **another person** does the action, that person appears: _las tortillas **que compra** doña Carmen_, _el bus **que tomo** cada mañana_.
1os2d2r: **Que** works for people, things and places and **never changes**. What changes is the verb, which agrees with the noun before it: _el niño que juega_, _los niños que juegan_.
24nps0: _Que_ already takes the place of _el libro_: don't repeat **lo**.
1ysliaw: After a noun and without commas you use **que**, for people too.
18pd5s9: From two sentences to one, and que versus qué
wuf4rs: To practise, think of two sentences that repeat a noun: _Tengo una amiga. **Mi amiga** vive en Santa Ana._ Remove the repeated noun, put **que** in its place and join everything: _Tengo una amiga **que** vive en Santa Ana._
1d9dh29: If the repeated noun is not the one doing the action, the rest of the sentence stays the same, but without _lo, la, los, las_: _Compré un mapa. Usé **el mapa** ayer._ → _Ayer usé el mapa **que** compré._
r8q4ct: Don't confuse **que** with **qué**. _Qué_, with an accent, asks: _¿**Qué** bus tomas?_ _Que_, without an accent, joins a noun and its detail: _El bus **que** tomo es el 51._
ajfdp7: Trick: if you can put the noun first and ask yourself "which one?", the answer starts with **que**: _¿Qué bus? El que va al centro._
ptmyw0: In Spanish **que** never disappears, even though in English you can drop _that_.
q0slfh: It isn't a question: **que** without an accent.
1os43l0: Donde for places, cuando for moments
z8k05w: After a **place** use **donde**: _el parque **donde** juegan los niños_, _la ciudad **donde** nací_. It means the same as _en el que / en la que_: _la plaza en la que nos vemos_.
oaofki: Compare: _el mercado **que** abre a las seis_ (the market does the action) and _el mercado **donde** compro fruta_ (I buy **at** the market). If inside the sentence you would say _in that place_, use **donde**.
1hv5huh: For a **moment** you have already named, use **cuando**: _En diciembre, **cuando** hace menos calor, vamos al lago._ With _el día, el año, el momento_ it is more natural to use **que** or **en que**: _el día **que** llegué_, _el año en que empecé_.
3uzjro: We meet **in** the square: it's a place, so use **donde**.
dmtfax: Lo que: an idea with no noun
163mmmd: **Lo que** doesn't come after a noun: it means _the thing that_ or _the things that_. Use it when you don't say the noun or you talk about an idea: _**Lo que** necesito es un mapa del centro._
1bqf7xd: It is very useful for giving opinions: _**Lo que** más me gusta de Santa Ana es el teatro_, _**Lo que** no entiendo es el horario del bus_. And also after a verb: _No sé **lo que** quiere_, _Haz **lo que** quieras_.
1x5h0iy: Compare: _la comida **que** prepara doña Carmen_ (there is a noun: _la comida_) and _**lo que** prepara doña Carmen_ (no noun: everything she makes).
1173k9q: To describe a word you can't remember, combine everything: _Es una cosa **que** sirve para…_, _Es el lugar **donde**…_, _Es **lo que** usas para…_
14qpb5u: With no noun before it you need **lo que**.
1oo8gvp: To say "the thing you say", the most natural option is **lo que**.

1tfu4i: The **que** of relative clauses is an **unstressed** word: it attaches to the next word and is barely heard. _la se-ño-ra-que-VEN-de-pan_. The same happens with **donde** and **cuando** inside the sentence.
8hcvsa: By contrast, **qué, dónde, cuándo** in questions are **stressed** and have a written accent: _¿QUÉ bus tomas?_, _¿DÓN-de vives?_ Your voice rises or hits that word.
746dvi: If you say the relative _que_ with a lot of stress, the sentence sounds like a question. Practise with long sentences: join the noun, the _que_ and the verb in a single breath group.
nqo5fb: Written accent only in questions and exclamations: **¿qué?, ¿dónde?, ¿cuándo?** No accent in relative clauses: **que, donde, cuando, lo que**.
